proof_summary: Take the composite number \(N=23492890653051=3\cdot37\cdot43\cdot42307\cdot116341\), whose five factors are distinct primes. Using \(\sum_{k=1}^n\gcd(k,n)=\sum_{d\mid n}d\varphi(n/d)\), the multiplicativity of this divisor sum, and its prime value \(2p-1\), one obtains \(\sum_{k=1}^N\gcd(k,N)=26N-1\); hence adding \(1\) gives \(26N\), so the relevant gcd is \(N\) and the quotient is \(1\) despite \(N\) being composite.
